inspiration: Modular dungeon as data: a dungeon is a list of rooms, each room a list of placed objects with a type, a position, a three-axis rotation and a bounding radius. Recreate with our own room grammar, our own object types and a theme field. Category-level: 'a room kit of placed props'. Reference: sql/dungeons/01_example_dungeon.json (structure only).

Factory chain on a planet: the planetary-industry tables hold pins (extractors and processors), links, routes and a planet record, so a colony is a graph of production nodes joined by routes. Recreate as a node graph with our own resource tiers and a flow map. Category-level: 'a colony production graph'. Reference: sql/dump.sh line 23 (table list) and the table names in sql/base (not read).

Claimable space with sovereignty: a migration adds the sovereignty tables and a later migration adds outposts, so claims and their holders are first-class data. Recreate with our own claim rules and upkeep costs. Category-level: 'a claimable outpost'. Reference: sql/migrations/20210409120025-sov.sql, sql/migrations/20211021144025-outpost.sql.

Agent and mission scaffolding: agent, offer and mission tables plus a skill-level table gate which missions an agent offers. Recreate as a mission board gated by our own skill tiers. Category-level only. Reference: sql/base agtAgents, agtOffers, agtMissions, agtSkillLevel (table names only; contents not read).

Character origin as data: ancestry, bloodline, career and background tables pick a start for a character. Recreate with our own origin set and no real-world ethnic or cultural names. Category-level only. Reference: sql/base chrAncestries, careers, chrBackgrounds (table names only).

Market history and orders: separate order, transaction and history tables feed a price view, and a dev note mentions the history dump needing a date fix. Recreate the loop (orders, history, price) with our own goods and our own date rules. Category-level only. Reference: doc/code_and_design_notes/Alasiya_TODO line 426 (note only).

briefs.label: Room-kit dungeon
briefs.why: A dungeon built from a few room templates with placed props reads quickly on a phone and is cheap to author. Signature structure: each room is a flat list of placed objects with a radius, so collision and spawns are simple.
briefs.keep: kept: a room is a list of placed objects with type, position, rotation and radius; rooms are the unit of authoring.
briefs.change: changed: our own room grammar (corridor, hall, vault), a theme field on each room, and door and exit nodes rather than bare objects. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy. Note: no visual asset in the box; the 375-wide silhouette test applies to the props we add later.

briefs.label: Colony production graph
briefs.why: A colony that is a visible chain (extract, process, route, deliver) gives players a reason to come back and a readable map. One signature behaviour: a route that carries goods between nodes on a clock.
briefs.keep: kept: a node graph of pins (extractors and processors) joined by links and routes.
briefs.change: changed: our own resource tiers and names, a map that shows flow as lanes rather than a table, and a timed delivery instead of a fixed launch. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.

briefs.label: Claimed outpost
briefs.why: A claimable structure that a group holds and must defend or pay for creates a visible territory on the map. One signature mechanic: an upkeep timer that a claim holder must refresh.
briefs.keep: kept: claim data as first-class tables (holder, claim, upkeep), plus a separate outpost layer added later.
briefs.change: changed: our own claim rules (kill-based, not payment-based), our own upkeep rhythm, and a structure silhouette of our own. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
